entry_points.text: Mount detachment gate does nothing for ordinary dentries and delegates mountpoint-marked dentries to full detachment.
Slow resolution and mount-aware stepping handle directories, mounts, and symlinks, with fast lock-free stepping for simple entries and slow handling otherwise.
Propagation replicates mounts across peer groups with capacity reservation, and path-based mount lookup retries under sequence protection until legitimized.

exports.text: Detach and mountpoint services clear stacked mounts from a dentry and record mount state, reporting missing, detached, non-mountable or busy cases and otherwise succeeding.
Propagation and teardown helpers privatize doomed sets, unlock counterparts, expand unmounts across peers, and release abandoned group identifiers.
Hashed lookup finds child mounts by parent plus dentry and child dentries by parent plus name, with name equality by bytes or parent operation, returning references or sequences for validation.
Parallel allocation converges lookups onto one pending dentry per name, and automount installation validates the returned tree, tolerates benign races, and grafts it as shrinkable.

hazards.text: Concurrent renames cause false absence requiring outer sequencing; mount counts enforce global maxima; copying refuses unbindable and namespace roots; atime updates need freeze protection and write access.

Control state uses mount flags for unmount, locked and sync teardown with transient shared, marked and candidate states, teardown modes, propagation modes with numeric groups, and dentry marks for mounted, compare, directory, symlink, miss and managed cases plus dead directory marking.

invariants.text: Unmount and detachment leave no live mount on the target, advance the namespace generation with coalesced notification, and drop namespace and parent visibility and pins.
Cover preservation is skipped for synchronous teardown and otherwise requires a doomed parent plus cover need or lock; preparation clears lock marks on propagation counterparts.
Propagation traversal prefers slave descent then climbs toward the origin; candidates are marked visited, blocking and locked chains resolved upward, survivors re-anchored with preserved mountpoints.

Mount and dentry lookup matches parent identity, hash, length and bytes plus hashed and sequence stability; directory character includes ordinary and automatic directories; names compare by words or bytes.

Slow allocation revalidates completed entries and completes pending ones via filesystem lookup with alias substitution; stepping honors no-crossing, normalizes automount directory results, and tracks jumps.

Attached state means present namespace with overmount chain; namespace files match paired operations; hardening adds timing lock and mirrors restrictions; pinning reuses linked entries and installation validates flags and busy state.

Identifier mappings share singletons without counting and free extended tables beyond embedded capacity on last release; teardown frees mapping, names and counters; symlink, negative and managed status derive from type and flags; atime refresh honors suppressions and relative-time rules; ancestor search walks upward with identity as containment.

locks.text: Detachment uses exclusive namespace and mount protection while dentry unhashing uses the dentry lock; hash walks use read-side sections with candidate locking or sequence retry.
Slow lookup holds the directory shared for the whole operation and refuses dead directories; shared protection maps to read acquire and release of the directory semaphore.
Exact mount locking uses auto-releasing pins with exclusive mount sequencing and a hash lock ordering propagation before publication; marking and subdir checks use rename and entry locks with retry.

state_machines.text: Privatization converges on surviving masters via peer and master traversal with temporary marks, then rewrites links, migrates slaves, and clears sharing and marks while releasing group identifiers.
Pending resolution moves from flagged fresh to published to waited to completed with wakeup and revalidation; lazy-to-referenced conversion validates sequences and references or requests retry.

Commit transfers detached subtrees into namespaces with capacity accounting and counter wakeup; group identities allocate positively with cleanup; RCU traversal follows stacks with validation; link resolution checks bans, refreshes time, and normalizes targets.

structs.text: Mountpoint records shard by mixed dentry address with pin lists; mounts form parent, child and sibling hierarchy; cover records link mountpoint and covered dentry until teardown.

Namespaces order mounts in a balanced tree by numeric identity with cached edges and visible sets; clones clear internal flags, inherit or clear group identity by mode, share mappings, and join peer and slave sets.
